excerpt: Grok 4.7, SpaceXAI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API as `grok-4.7`.
Agentic coding with Grok Build (grok-4.7), our coding model, on the API and CLI.
Generate text, have conversations, use tools, and build AI-powered applications.
Convert text to natural speech or transcribe audio with our voice models.
When using supported schema features, the response is guaranteed to match your schema.
Realtime Multi-agent Research enables Grok to orchestrate multiple AI agents that work together in real time to perform deep, multi-step research tasks.
Some models allow images in the input. The model will consider the image context when generating the response.
The xAI API supports **tool calling**, enabling Grok to perform actions beyond generating text—like searching the web, executing code, querying your data, or calling your own custom functions.
Define custom tools that the model can invoke during a conversation. The model requests the call, you execute it locally, and return the result.
The Web Search tool enables Grok to search the web in real-time and browse web pages to find information.
The code execution tool enables Grok to write and execute Python code in real-time, dramatically expanding its capabilities beyond text generation.
Remote MCP Tools allow Grok to connect to external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, extending its capabilities with custom tools from third parties or your own implementations.

The collections search tool enables Grok to search through your uploaded knowledge bases (collections), allowing it to retrieve relevant information from your documents to provide more accurate and contextually relevant responses.
When consecutive requests share the same starting messages, the xAI API automatically caches them.
The Batch API lets you process large volumes of requests asynchronously with reduced pricing and higher rate limits.
Priority Processing gives your xAI API requests higher scheduling priority, which typically results in lower time-to-first-token (TTFT) and faster inter-token latency (ITL)
If you need API request handling and model inference to happen in the United States, use the US regional endpoint, `https://us.api.x.ai/v1`.
Every inference response from the xAI API includes the exact cost you were charged for that request, returned via a `cost_in_usd_ticks` field

the following models will be retired from the xAI API... requests to the retired model slugs above will automatically redirect to `grok-4.3`. The slugs themselves continue to resolve, so you do not need to change your code
The xAI REST API is compatible with the OpenAI REST API.
The xAI gRPC API exposes the same models and services as the REST API over gRPC.
Access xAI's Grok models through Google Cloud's managed platform with enterprise security, governance, and unified billing.
Grok models on Foundry give you strong reasoning, native tool use, enterprise authentication through Microsoft Entra ID, Azure-native monitoring, and an OpenAI-compatible API.
xAI hosts a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI assistants and agents direct access to the xAI documentation.
For teams that require stricter data handling, see [Zero Data Retention (ZDR)](#what-is-zero-data-retention-zdr) below.
Grok can search through and reason over documents you attach to chat messages... the system automatically activates the `attachment_search` tool and transforms your request into an agentic workflow.
Collections offers xAI API users a robust set of tools and methods to seamlessly integrate their enterprise requirements and internal knowledge bases with the xAI API.
Generate images from text prompts with Grok Imagine models. The API supports batch generation of multiple images, and control over aspect ratio, resolution, and quality.
Edit an existing image by providing a source image along with your prompt. The model understands the image content and applies your requested changes.
Use up to five source images for a single image edit.
Generate videos from text prompts with Grok video models. The API supports configurable duration, aspect ratio, and resolution
Transform a still image into a video by providing a source image along with an optional prompt. The model animates the image content based on your instructions.
Provide reference images, a preset voice, or both to guide the generated video... useful for virtual try-on, product placement, character-consistent storytelling, and voice identity.
`grok-imagine-video` delivers high-fidelity edits with strong scene preservation, modifying only what you ask for while keeping the rest of the video intact
Extend an existing video by providing a source video and a text prompt describing what should happen next. The result is a single video that picks up seamlessly from the last frame
Convert text into spoken audio with a single API call. The API supports a rich set of expressive voices, inline speech tags for fine-grained delivery control
Transcribe audio files into text with a single API call, or stream audio in real time over WebSocket. The API supports 12 audio formats, word-level timestamps, multichannel transcription
Clone a voice from a short reference clip and use it anywhere a built-in voice works. Upload an audio sample and immediately start using it in our TTS and Speech to Speech APIs.

Ephemeral tokens provide secure, short-lived authentication for client-side applications. Use them when connecting to the Speech to Speech API from browsers or mobile apps to avoid exposing your API key.
The Management API serves as a dedicated interface to the xAI platform, empowering developers and teams to programmatically manage their xAI API teams.

Grok does good research and produces less bullshit, especially when prompted to be critical of an idea, compared to qwen, deepseek, and gemini on same prompts via openrouter
Grok will end tasks almost immediately and claim 'Done!'. It's definitely the laziest and most 'dishonest' of all the models. I can't use Grok for any serious coding task.
Having used Grok for personal chat: it's by far the worst one amongst Claude, ChatGPT, Deepseek, Gemini. The personality is bland and it doesn't work nearly as hard or even tries to help.
If you ask Grok about Elon Musk's mother's AI-edited birthday photos, it will always take Elon's defense and vehemently deny any wrongdoing even when confronted with contrary evidence.

In my experience Grok 4.5 codes at Opus 4.8 level, and being much faster and cheaper, self-review makes final code better than Opus 4.8 for the same time/budget. But Opus was better for non-code architecture discussions.
In my tests Grok 4.5 is definitely not Opus level. It is somewhere in between Sonnet and Opus, I'd say maybe a bit closer to Sonnet. We'll see with 4.6.

I've been using Grok instead of Opus the past few weeks. It's a downgrade, but barely noticeable for me and totally inconsequential for the amount of work required to fix it and the corresponding $$$ saving.

I like Grok, but I don't think that it's quite Fable-tier. It's good, but I think it occupies a position on the Pareto frontier a little more toward the 'cheap' side and less toward the 'intelligence' side.

I've been using Grok Build over the last couple weeks. It's actually a very good CLI. The Grok Build 0.1 model isn't great but can also use Composer 2.5 which is excellent. Well worth trying.
Grok has an order of magnitude less OpenRouter usage than Claude, GPT, even Gemini, used as a rough proxy for popularity of closed-source models.
Aside from a brief window last summer Grok has been behind the curve for coding, and before the Cursor acquisition they didn't have a harness. Now they have an Opus-tier model and a real harness.
This is the first grok model that seems actually pretty competitive at SWE, unlike previous ones which were vastly outclassed by other models.

Pricing docs publish per-model token prices without sales contact: "All prices are in USD", a Text API Pricing table of input / cached input / output prices per 1M tokens per model (e.g. "grok-4.7 (< 200k prompt tokens) | 500k | $2.00 | $0.50 | $6.00"), with the long-context billing rule stated ("requests whose prompt reaches the listed token threshold are billed at the higher rate for all tokens in the request").

Context windows documented per model: the grok-4.7 model page states "Context window: 500,000 tokens" under "At a glance", and the models/pricing tables carry a Context column per model (500k for grok-4.7/4.6/4.5, 1M for grok-4.3 and the grok-4.20 family, 256k for grok-build-0.1).

A dedicated Rate Limits page documents per-model requests-per-second and tokens-per-minute caps at every tier ("grok-4.7 | T0: 150, T1: 172, T2: 208, T3: 312, T4: 500 | T0: 50M ... T4: 100M"), spend-based tier thresholds ($0/$50/$250/$1,000/$5,000), 429 semantics ("Exceeding any limit returns a `429 Too Many Requests` error"), and per-team limits viewable in the xAI Console.

Programmatic catalog discovery documented in the REST reference: "GET /v1/models — List all models available to the authenticating API key, including model names (ID), creation times, and pricing", with a documented response schema carrying `aliases`, `context_length`, per-token prices, and a `capabilities` object (including accepted `reasoning_effort` values).

Per-model spec pages published: the grok-4.7 page documents modalities ("text, image → text"), context window, capability flags ("Function calling: Yes; Structured outputs: Yes; Reasoning: Yes; Reasoning efforts (supported): `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`"), pricing, and Batch API support status — a specification card, not a safety/system card.

Model lifecycle handled via dated migration guides: "Grok Model Retirement on May 15, 2026" retires named slugs (grok-4-fast-*, grok-4-0709, grok-code-fast-1, grok-3, ...) with advance notice, an automatic redirect policy ("requests to the retired model slugs above will automatically redirect to `grok-4.3`. The slugs themselves continue to resolve, so you do not need to change your code to avoid breakage"), and a documented pricing impact.

A "Model Aliases" section documents the versioning scheme: "`<modelname>` is aliased to the latest stable version. `<modelname>-latest` is aliased to the latest version" — moving aliases for auto-migration alongside pinned versioned model IDs.

Reasoning controls documented: "`grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6`, and `grok-4.5` support the `reasoning_effort` parameter, which controls how much effort the model spends thinking before responding. If not specified, `reasoning_effort` defaults to `\"high\"`. Reasoning cannot be disabled." Accepted values `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh` with runnable examples.

Self-serve start documented in the quickstart: "Sign up for an account at console.x.ai, then load it with credits to start using the API. ... Create an API key via the API Keys page, then export it or add it as an environment variable" — no sales contact required, followed by a runnable first request (curl/Python/JavaScript) in the same guide.

Per-request spend visibility built into the API: "Every inference response from the xAI API includes the exact cost you were charged for that request, returned via a `cost_in_usd_ticks` field in the `usage` object ... This is the actual amount billed, after all applicable discounts"; the management API additionally "facilitates oversight of billing aspects, including monitoring prepaid credit balances and usage".

Retention controls documented in the security FAQ: a default 30-day retention plus self-serve Zero Data Retention ("ZDR ensures that API request inputs (i.e., your prompt) and outputs ... are never persisted to disk"), toggleable per team in Team Settings, with programmatic confirmation ("every API response includes an `x-zero-data-retention` header set to `\"true\"` or `\"false\"`").
